title.en: The Parliamentary system: legislature and executive

text.en: Visitors to the new Parliament building see walls with carvings of peacocks, lotuses, tribal art, temple patterns and freedom fighters. It feels like a museum of India. What happens inside it?

India is a parliamentary democracy, where the people elect representatives who form the government.
The government has three organs: the legislature makes laws, the executive carries them out, and the judiciary interprets them.
The Parliament is the supreme legislative body and consists of the President, the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha.
The Lok Sabha is the House of the People, elected directly by citizens, with a maximum of 550 members, and a term of five years.
The Rajya Sabha is the Council of States, whose members are elected indirectly by state legislators and it is a permanent House, with one-third of its members retiring every two years.
The President is the head of state and the nominal executive, and the Prime Minister with the Council of Ministers forms the real executive.
The party or alliance with a majority in the Lok Sabha forms the government, and its leader becomes Prime Minister.
The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha and must resign if it loses the House's confidence.
In each state, the Governor is the head, the Chief Minister leads the government, and the Legislative Assembly makes state laws.
Parliament makes laws, passes the budget and keeps a check on the government through questions and debates.

problem.en: How is the Prime Minister chosen?

text.en: People elect members of the Lok Sabha.
The party with a majority forms the government.
The leader of that party is appointed Prime Minister by the President.

prompt.en: Why is the Council of Ministers responsible to the Lok Sabha?

requiredIdeas.en: The Lok Sabha is elected by the people.
If it is lost, they must resign.

points.en: Parliament = President + Lok Sabha + Rajya Sabha.
The Lok Sabha is directly elected; the Rajya Sabha indirectly.
The Prime Minister heads the executive with majority support.
